D_server_side_logic.additional_logic:
1. Third-party endpoint observations report search-flight as read-only, idempotent, and open-world; feedback-to-devs as writable, non-idempotent, and open-world. Official Kiwi docs provide no tool annotations.
2. No server-enforced confirmation flow was found. Search is described as returning booking links; the purchase is completed on Kiwi.com. A third-party observation reports feedback transmission without confirmation.
3. Official setup instructions do not require server credentials. No OAuth scopes, role inheritance, server admin switch, allowlist, redirect approval, token lifetime, or revocation policy was found. Client workspace admins may control connector setup.
4. One global root endpoint is documented. No read-only URL mode, toolsets, filters, query-free mode, sandbox, or regional variants were found.
5. Kiwi’s article says only searches (dates, destinations, passenger count) are shared, while the user’s AI conversations stay private. No field masking or server-side PII filter was documented. A third-party catalogue reports feedback as free text, so content boundaries are advisory.
6. Official MCP rate limits and per-call costs were not found. A third-party endpoint observation reports 15 itineraries per search and no pagination or result limit parameter; a reported feedback input is capped at 3,000 characters.
7. Official parameter schemas and validation behavior were not published. A third-party observation reports typed schemas and Pydantic validation messages, but no evidence of operator overrides or automatic argument correction.
8. No MCP-specific audit trail, per-call logging, telemetry disclosure, or opt-out was found in the official pages reviewed.
9. Third-party catalogues report feedback-to-devs as a channel for flight-search feedback to Kiwi developers. Official Kiwi docs do not list it. Search results include Kiwi booking links; Kiwi describes checkout as a separate user action. No upsell response was found in the tool reference.
10. Kiwi’s tool page gives the model use and display guidance; this is documented as descriptions, not server-enforced behavior. No server-delivered skill tool was found. The official repository is install documentation, not code.
11. Kiwi says the assistant can remember user preferences within the planning conversation. This describes assistant context; server-side memory or state affecting later calls is not documented.
12. One flat endpoint is documented; no subservers or dynamic toolsets were found. A single search tool and a catalogue-reported feedback tool do not establish a nested architecture.
13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or general request tool was found in the official list or catalogued endpoint list.

E_aggregated.action_count: 2 reported for the endpoint: 1 official and 1 catalogue-only
E_aggregated.action_count_comment: Kiwi’s official MCP page (https://www.kiwi.com/en/pages/mcp/) names 1 tool, search-flight, and states a single-tool total. No official schema list was published. I added feedback-to-devs after it appeared in endpoint reports on MCP.so, Agentman, Anchor Terminal, and ConnectorReport; each reports 2 tools. ToolJunction reports 1. The Claude connector page listed in links.json returned 404. The added tool is labelled third-party because no official Kiwi source names it.

actions.description: Search Kiwi.com flight inventory and return matching itineraries with booking links.
Transmit flight-search feedback, bug reports, or feature requests to Kiwi.com developers.

E_aggregated.token_method: No implementation code or verbatim complete official tool definitions and initialize instructions were available to serialize. The public repository contains installation documentation only; third-party descriptions are insufficient for a reproducible token count.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The MCP list provides flight search and reported feedback only. Booking, payment, and checkout are completed by following a result link to Kiwi.com; Kiwi’s official article describes the connector as displaying flights in chat and directing users to Kiwi.com to complete purchase. No MCP booking or payment tool is documented. Sources: https://www.kiwi.com/en/pages/mcp/ ; https://www.kiwi.com/stories/kiwi-mcp-connector/

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Kiwi recommends detailed prompts with passenger counts, budget, dates, and timing preferences for more relevant results. It gives examples of comparing cheapest and fastest options and of stating family or timing constraints. These are user/client instructions; no corresponding server enforcement is documented. Source: https://www.kiwi.com/stories/kiwi-mcp-connector/
F_documentation.governance_promises: Kiwi states: “Only your flight searches: dates, destinations, how many passengers. Your actual AI conversations stay private.” The article also says “Same prices, same protections” and that booking links lead to normal Kiwi.com checkout, support, and guarantees. Source: https://www.kiwi.com/stories/kiwi-mcp-connector/
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Kiwi describes the connector as free, providing real flight options in chat, with booking links and the same prices and protections as booking directly. Source: https://www.kiwi.com/stories/kiwi-mcp-connector/
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The documented flow supports searching and handing off to Kiwi.com checkout. The privacy statement does not specify server retention, logs, subprocessors, or handling of feedback text. No code is available to compare these statements with implementation. The third-party-reported feedback tool accepts a separate message to developers, which is not addressed by the quoted search-data promise.

contradictions: Kiwi’s official MCP page says the server “exposes a single tool: search-flight”; MCP.so, Agentman, Anchor Terminal, and ConnectorReport report two endpoint tools, adding feedback-to-devs. The extra tool is not in the official list. Sources: https://www.kiwi.com/en/pages/mcp/ ; https://mcp.so/servers/kiwi ; https://agentman.ai/agentskills/connections/mcp-server/kiwi-com ; https://www.anchorterminal.com/tools/kiwi-mcp ; https://connectorreport.com/c/kiwi

Kiwi’s official page advertises date flexibility up to plus or minus three days. Anchor Terminal reports a live schema allowing departure and return flexibility parameters from 0 to 10 days. Source: https://www.kiwi.com/en/pages/mcp/ ; https://www.anchorterminal.com/tools/kiwi-mcp

Kiwi’s official page says “search and book flights,” while its article describes the MCP flow as displaying flight options and sending users to Kiwi.com to complete purchase. No booking tool is listed in the official tool list. Sources: https://www.kiwi.com/en/pages/mcp/ ; https://www.kiwi.com/stories/kiwi-mcp-connector/
observations_for_research: The official MCP page’s stated tool count differs from several third-party reports of the live endpoint; the additional reported tool transmits feedback to the vendor.
Kiwi’s article describes the assistant as retaining travel preferences in the conversation, while the server’s own memory behavior is undocumented.
The public repository is an installation-instructions README rather than implementation code, so hosted behavior cannot be compared with source.
notes: Checked links.json, links_check.txt, pages/ and code/. No Kiwi-owned server implementation, package, or registry entry was found in the prepared evidence. The official README repository was inspected on GitHub and contains installation instructions, not executable code. Official pages do not publish MCP schemas, full tool parameters, annotations, initialize instructions, or a current release status. Third-party catalogues were used only to cross-check and add the reported feedback-to-devs tool; their endpoint and schema observations are identified as third-party evidence. The supplied OAuth probe and well-known responses were used as provided.
